citation.authors: Kostis JB, Kim HJ, Rusnak J, Casale T et al

cited_by.title: How some medicines work differently by gene

record.population: 12,557 people with hypertension in a randomised, double-blind trial of enalapril 5 to 40 mg daily
record.design: Prospective ascertainment and expert adjudication of angioedema within a randomised controlled trial
record.finding: Angioedema occurred in 86 people (0.68%). Black race (odds ratio 2.88, 95% CI 1.72 to 4.82), history of drug rash (3.78), age over 65 (1.60) and seasonal allergies (1.79) were independent risk factors. Incidence was 3.6 per 1,000 patients per month soon after starting and fell to 0.4. Fatal angioedema or angioedema needing airway protection did not occur.
record.note: A trial population of mixed ancestry, with race as a stand-in for unmeasured genes; abstract read in full.
